---
title: "Run, sync and check"
---

```{python}
#| include: false
# Setup, hidden from readers. Every .qmd page starts with this same cell
# (tests/test_docs_pages.py checks). It works in a fresh folder, reads the
# example project from this repository's tests/data (offline), and defines
# sh(), which runs a command shown on the page and prints its output.
import os
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import warnings
from pathlib import Path

import useful_views

_mirror = Path(useful_views.__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "tests" / "data"
if not (_mirror / "examples" / "pwt").is_dir():
    raise RuntimeError(f"no example data at {_mirror}")
os.environ["USEFUL_VIEWS_DATA_URL"] = str(_mirror)
os.environ.update(NO_COLOR="1", PYTHON_COLORS="0", COLUMNS="100", PYTHONUNBUFFERED="1", PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8")
WORK = str(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="useful-views-docs-")).resolve())
os.chdir(WORK)
warnings.formatwarning = lambda message, category, *args, **kwargs: f"{category.__name__}: {message}\n"


def sh(line, expect=0):
    """Run one command shown on the page (useful-views, cd or cat) and print
    its output as a terminal would. Fails if it exits with another code."""
    word, _, rest = line.partition(" ")
    if word == "cd":
        os.chdir(shlex.split(rest)[0])
        return
    if word == "cat":
        print(Path(shlex.split(rest)[0]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"), end="")
        return
    if word != "useful-views":
        raise ValueError(f"sh() runs useful-views, cd and cat, not {line!r}")
    done = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "useful_views", *shlex.split(rest)],
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
    )
    out = done.stdout.replace(WORK, "/path/to")
    if out.strip():
        print(out, end="")
    if done.returncode != expect:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{line!r} exited with {done.returncode}, not {expect}:\n{out}")
```

This page shows what `run`, `sync` and `check` do, and what to run after
you change something. `run` and `sync` differ the way `uv run` and `uv sync`
do. `run` does the one recipe you name, now. `sync` brings the whole project
in line with its recipe folders. `check` reports, and changes nothing.

Before you `run` or `sync` a project you didn't write, read
[Steps are code](steps.md#steps-are-code).

## Make the views

Get the example project, make its views, and check them:

```sh
useful-views example pwt
cd pwt-example
useful-views sync
useful-views check
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
sh("useful-views example pwt")
sh("cd pwt-example")
sh("useful-views sync")
sh("useful-views check")
```

`sync` makes the project match its recipe folders, the way `uv sync` makes
an environment match its lock file. It:

1. checks every recipe against the [rules](../reference/rules.md), judging
   each against the records as they will be when its turn comes. If any
   recipe would be refused, it lists every problem and changes nothing. A
   folder with no `recipe.toml` is skipped, with a warning.
2. removes the records of deleted recipe folders, and of views a recipe no
   longer lists, with their files. It warns about recipes that read a
   removed view.
3. runs, upstream first, each recipe that has never run, whose
   `recipe.toml` or steps have changed, whose views are missing, or that
   read a view made again with different data since. Then it runs every
   recipe downstream of those.

Records only ever come from real runs. `useful-views sync --all` runs every
recipe.

### If sync stops

Before it runs anything, `sync` removes the views of each recipe it will run
after another one it reads from. If a recipe fails, or `sync` is
interrupted, it stops there:

- the recipes that ran stay recorded;
- the views it hadn't made again are missing, however it stopped (even if
  the process was killed), so the next `sync` makes them;
- the message says what it did, what it didn't reach, and what to run next.

## Check the project

Change the description in `recipes/pwt_panel/recipe.toml`, then check:

```{python}
#| include: false
# Change the recipe's description, as you would in an editor. Remember the
# panel's data hash and when gdp-per-capita.parquet was made, for the
# asserts after the next sync.
toml = Path("recipes/pwt_panel/recipe.toml")
text = toml.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
assert "Country-year panel of core" in text
toml.write_text(text.replace("Country-year panel of core", "Country-year panel of the core"), encoding="utf-8")
panel_hash = useful_views.data_hash("useful-views/pwt-panel.parquet")
gdp_made = os.stat("useful-views/gdp-per-capita.parquet").st_mtime_ns
```

```sh
useful-views check
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
sh("useful-views check", expect=1)
```

```{python}
#| include: false
# What the text says; the build fails if it stops being true.
assert {f.recipe: f.reason for f in useful_views.check()} == {"pwt_panel": "changed", "gdp_per_capita": "upstream"}
```

`check` reports the recipe you changed, and the recipe downstream of it.
Each finding says what to do about it. `check` works out the same plan as
`sync`, so a clean `check` means `sync` has nothing to refuse.
[Check findings](../reference/check-findings.md) lists every kind of
finding.

`check` exits with 1 when it finds anything, so it works as a gate in
scripts. In CI, it needs the raw data and a `sync` first. A plain git
checkout has no raw files or views, so `check` reports them missing there.
Gate that job with `useful-views cookbook --check` instead
([Cookbook](cookbook.md#check-it-in-ci)).

Now sync again:

```sh
useful-views sync
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
sh("useful-views sync")
```

```{python}
#| include: false
# What the text says; the build fails if it stops being true.
assert useful_views.data_hash("useful-views/pwt-panel.parquet") == panel_hash
assert os.stat("useful-views/gdp-per-capita.parquet").st_mtime_ns != gdp_made
assert useful_views.check() == []
```

`sync` ran both recipes, though the panel's data came out the same. Data
that comes out the same doesn't show that the recipes reading it would give
the same results. A step can see what a data hash leaves out, such as a time
zone's name or a column's categories. So `sync` never skips a recipe
downstream of one it runs.

## Run one recipe

```{python}
#| include: false
record = Path("datapackage.json").read_bytes()
catalog = Path("useful-views/README.md").read_bytes()
```

```sh
useful-views run pwt_panel
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
sh("useful-views run pwt_panel")
```

```{python}
#| include: false
# What the text says; the build fails if it stops being true.
assert Path("datapackage.json").read_bytes() == record
assert Path("useful-views/README.md").read_bytes() == catalog
```

`run` warns that `gdp_per_capita` reads the views it just made. The panel
came out the same, so `datapackage.json` and the catalog are unchanged, byte
for byte.

`run` checks the recipe against the rules before it changes anything. Then
it:

1. deletes the recipe's views and empties `work/<recipe>/`, so a leftover
   file can never pass for a fresh result;
2. runs each step in order, showing its output as it runs, in a terminal or
   a notebook cell. The first step that fails stops the run.
3. checks that every declared view was written as a non-empty parquet file;
4. records the run in `datapackage.json` and the catalog. Only this
   recipe's entries change.

If a step fails or a view is missing, nothing is recorded, and the recipe's
views are removed. Its record from the last successful run is kept, and
`check` reports the views as missing, or the recipe as never run. The files
in `work/<recipe>/` stay as the steps left them, so you can see how far the
run got.

`run` never runs other recipes. If the recipe reads another recipe's view,
run that recipe before it, or use `sync`, which runs recipes in order. When
other recipes read the views `run` made, it warns and names them:

- **Different data:** they are out of date. `check` reports them
  (`input-data-changed`), and `sync` runs them.
- **The same data:** `sync` doesn't run them. Run them too if you changed
  how the data is stored, such as a time zone's name, a column's storage
  type or unit, or its categories. The warning gives the command.
- **Can't tell:** the records are from before fingerprints, a view has no
  data hash, or a fingerprint is one this version doesn't understand. `run`
  says which, and to use `useful-views sync --all`.

Sort the rows of each view before writing it, by columns that together
identify each row. The same rows in another order have another
[fingerprint](../guides/fingerprints.qmd), so the recipes downstream would
look out of date after every run.

## What to run after a change

| When you | Run |
|---|---|
| add a recipe or a step, or edit a `recipe.toml` | `useful-views sync` |
| edit the code inside a step, or a helper module | `useful-views run <recipe>`, then what it says to run next. Or `useful-views sync --all`. |
| replace a file in `raw/` under the same name | `useful-views sync --all`. Or `run` each recipe that reads it, then what each run says. Or give the new file a new name, and change the path in `inputs` and in the step that reads it. Then `sync` notices. |
| edit `sources.toml` | `useful-views sync`. It runs no recipe (see [Sources](sources.md)). |
| `git pull`, merge or switch branches | `useful-views sync --all`. The views aren't in git, so they still come from the recipes as they were. |
| delete a recipe folder, or remove an output | `useful-views sync`. It removes the old records and view files. First change the inputs of any recipe that reads those views. |
| rename a recipe folder | Change `work/<old name>/` to `work/<new name>/` in its steps, then `useful-views sync`. |
| clone the project on another computer | Install the libraries, place the raw files, then `useful-views sync`. |
| finish a change you will commit | `useful-views sync`, then `useful-views cookbook`, then commit. |

`sync` and `check` don't notice an edit to a step's code or a raw file's
contents until that recipe runs again, nor old views left by a `git pull`.
See [Stale views](stale-views.md), and
[#32](https://github.com/jameshorine/useful-views/issues/32) for the plan.

## One command at a time

`run`, `sync` and `cookbook` (when it writes) take a lock on the project. A
second one started meanwhile is refused, saying another command is changing
the project. Wait, then run it again. `check`, `rules` and `cookbook
--check` don't take the lock. The lock file, `work/.useful-views.lock`, is
all a refused `run` or `sync` leaves behind. See
[Environment](../reference/environment.md#stopping-a-command).
